top_articles.title: EvoSafeHarness: Evolving Model- and Domain-Specific Harnesses for Securing Agents
top_articles.summary: Researchers introduced EvoSafeHarness, an automated optimization framework designed to synthesize system-level safety harnesses for frozen language model agents. Unlike static expert-written guardrails that cause utility degradation or security gaps, EvoSafeHarness jointly optimizes natural-language policy guidelines and executable inspection logic tailored to specific model-domain pairings. The system evaluates runtime behavior, environment specifications, and adversarial context reviews to enforce application-aware state governance. Across evaluation suites, it significantly improves the safety-utility trade-off. On DecodingTrust-Agent, it lowered attack success rates from 45.6% to 10.0% with a minor 3.3-point utility loss. Additionally, on AgentDojo, it sustained 82.8% utility with 0% attack success, doubling the performance of existing solutions like CaMeL.

top_articles.title: TempCloze: Can Video-LLMs Identify the Missing Middle?
top_articles.summary: Researchers introduced TempCloze, a visual-first cloze benchmark designed to evaluate temporal reasoning in Video-LLMs without language-shortcut biases. Given the opening and closing video segments of a scene, models must select the correct missing middle clip from four candidates. TempCloze comprises 1,521 filtered egocentric and long-take videos from seven datasets, featuring distractor options carefully selected along semantic, temporal alignment, and progression dimensions to eliminate visual appearance cues. Testing across 10 proprietary and 21 open-source Video-LLMs revealed temporal alignment as the main bottleneck for current models. While models recognize plausible semantic events, they struggle with chronological ordering and context direction sensitivity.
